faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution vests the power of superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission?
The Election Commission is common to which of the following?

options.a: Neither, since it is autonomous of both
options.b: Both the Central and state governments

faqs.a: Both the Central and state governments

faqs.q: Elections to which of the following are NOT within the jurisdiction of the Election Commission of India?
faqs.e: Elections to panchayats and municipalities fall under the separate State Election Commission.

faqs.q: Who determines the number of election commissioners in the Election Commission?
When more than one election commissioner is appointed, who acts as the chairman of the Election Commission?
Regional commissioners to assist the Election Commission are appointed by the President after consultation with whom?
Since its inception in 1950, the Election Commission functioned as a single-member body until which date?

Consider the following statements regarding the strength of the Election Commission:
(I) Two more election commissioners were first appointed on 16 October 1989
(II) The two posts of election commissioners were abolished in January 1990
(III) Two more election commissioners were appointed again in October 1993
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Since October 1993, the Election Commission has continued functioning as a three-member body.

faqs.q: The appointment of two additional election commissioners in 1989 was necessitated mainly on account of which development?

options.c: Lowering of the voting age from 21 to 18 years

faqs.a: Lowering of the voting age from 21 to 18 years

faqs.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
faqs.e: The 61st Amendment Act of 1988 came into force in 1989.

faqs.q: Under the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, in what year was this Act enacted?
As per the Election Commission (Conditions of Service) Act, 1991, the salary and perquisites of the Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners are similar to those of whom?

options.b: A judge of the Supreme Court
options.c: A judge of a High Court

faqs.a: A judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.q: In case of a difference of opinion among the election commissioners, how is the matter decided?

options.b: By the Chief Election Commissioner alone

faqs.q: What is the term of office of an election commissioner under the 1991 Act?

options.a: Six years with no age limit
options.b: Five years with no age limit
options.c: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.d: Five years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.a: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as which authority?

options.b: A Judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.a: A Judge of the Supreme Court
faqs.e: Removal requires a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with special majority, on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

faqs.q: An election commissioner other than the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only on the recommendation of whom?

Consider the following statements regarding constitutional flaws in safeguarding the Election Commission's independence:
(I) The Constitution has not prescribed qualifications for members of the Election Commission
(II) The Constitution has not specified the term of members of the Election Commission
(III) The Constitution has debarred retiring election commissioners from further government appointment
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Constitution has NOT debarred retiring election commissioners from further appointment by the government — this is itself cited as a flaw.

faqs.q: In which case did the Supreme Court give directions on the appointment process of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?
faqs.e: Decided in 2023.

faqs.q: As per the Anoop Baranwal case (2023), the committee recommending appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners consists of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and which other member?

options.c: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
options.d: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

faqs.a: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha

faqs.q: According to the Supreme Court's Anoop Baranwal ruling, until when shall its directions on Election Commission appointments remain in effect?

options.c: Until Parliament makes a law in consonance with Article 324
options.d: Until the President issues fresh rules

faqs.a: Until Parliament makes a law in consonance with Article 324

faqs.q: The powers and functions of the Election Commission are classified into Administrative, Advisory and which other category?
The Election Commission determines territorial areas of electoral constituencies on the basis of which Act?
Which of the following is a Quasi-Judicial function of the Election Commission?

options.b: Advising the President on MP disqualifications
options.c: Acting as a court to settle disputes on recognition of political parties

faqs.a: Acting as a court to settle disputes on recognition of political parties

faqs.q: The Election Commission advises the President on disqualification matters concerning members of which body?
faqs.e: The Commission advises the Governor on disqualification matters relating to members of the state legislature.

faqs.q: On matters relating to disqualification of members of the state legislature, the Election Commission advises whom?
The Election Commission can advise the President on holding elections in a state under President's Rule for which purpose?

options.a: To extend the period of emergency after one year

faqs.a: To extend the period of emergency after one year

faqs.q: The Election Commission grants political parties the status of national or state parties on the basis of what?
At the state level, the Election Commission is assisted by the chief electoral officer, who is appointed by whom?

options.a: The Chief Election Commissioner in consultation with the state government

faqs.a: The Chief Election Commissioner in consultation with the state government

faqs.q: At the district level, who acts as the district returning officer?
faqs.e: The Collector, as district returning officer, appoints a returning officer for every constituency and a presiding officer for every polling booth.

faqs.q: How many Delimitation Commission Acts has the Parliament made so far?
faqs.e: The Delimitation Commission Acts were made in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002.

faqs.q: The Constitution provides for a separate State Election Commission for panchayats and municipalities under which Constitutional Amendment Acts?
faqs.e: These Amendment Acts of 1992 introduced the State Election Commission for local body elections.

faqs.q: As of 2018, the salary of a judge of the Supreme Court (to which the Chief Election Commissioner's salary is equated) was fixed at what amount per month?

Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission's power to cancel polls:
(I) It can cancel polls in the event of rigging
(II) It can cancel polls in the event of booth capturing
(III) It can cancel polls only with prior approval of the President
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The rigging, booth capturing, violence and other irregularities as grounds for cancelling polls, with no requirement of prior Presidential approval.

faqs.q: Which of the following is NOT among the guiding principles laid down by the Election Commission for itself?

options.a: Adopting technology for improvement of the electoral process
options.b: Fixing the retirement age of election commissioners
options.d: Building quality infrastructure for smooth conduct of elections

faqs.a: Fixing the retirement age of election commissioners
faqs.e: Guiding principles relate to governance values and conduct of elections, not to service conditions of commissioners, which are governed separately by statute.

faqs.q: The Union Public Service Commission is dealt with under which Part of the Constitution?
Which range of Articles contains provisions regarding the composition, appointment, removal, independence, powers and functions of the UPSC?
Who appoints the chairman and members of the UPSC?
The Constitution requires what proportion of UPSC members to have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a state?
What is the term of office of the chairman and members of the UPSC?

options.b: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.c: Six years with no age limit
options.d: Five years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.a: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.q: To whom does a chairman or member of the UPSC address their resignation?

options.a: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the acting chairman of the UPSC:
(I) The President can appoint an acting chairman when the office of chairman falls vacant
(II) The President can appoint an acting chairman when the chairman is unable to perform functions due to absence
(III) The acting chairman must be appointed from outside the Commission
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The acting chairman is appointed from among the existing members of the UPSC, not from outside.

faqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a ground on which the President can remove the chairman or a member of the UPSC?

options.a: Difference of opinion with the government
options.b: Engaging in paid employment outside official duties during the term

faqs.a: Difference of opinion with the government

faqs.q: For removal of a UPSC chairman or member on the ground of misbehaviour, the President must refer the matter for enquiry to which body?
faqs.e: The advice tendered by the Supreme Court in this regard is binding on the President.

faqs.q: During the pendency of a Supreme Court enquiry into misbehaviour of a UPSC member, what power does the President have?

options.c: Transfer the member to an SPSC

faqs.q: Under the Constitution, the chairman or a member of the UPSC is deemed guilty of "misbehaviour" if they are concerned or interested in what?

options.a: Any private business unrelated to government
options.d: Any contract or agreement made by the Government of India or a state

faqs.a: Any contract or agreement made by the Government of India or a state

faqs.q: The salaries, allowances and pensions of the UPSC chairman, members and staff are charged on which fund?
faqs.e: Being charged expenditure, they are not subject to vote of Parliament.

faqs.q: After ceasing to hold office, the chairman of the UPSC is not eligible for further employment under which authority?

options.b: The Government of India or a state

faqs.a: The Government of India or a state

faqs.q: A member of the UPSC (on ceasing to hold office) is eligible for appointment as the chairman of which body/bodies?

options.a: Neither, as members cannot be reappointed

faqs.q: Is the chairman or a member of the UPSC eligible for a second term after completing their first term?

options.a: No, they are not eligible for reappointment
options.b: Yes, but only as acting chairman

faqs.a: No, they are not eligible for reappointment

faqs.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the office of Governor is a 'constitutional office' and not employment under the government, thereby validating a former UPSC chairman's appointment as Governor?
Which of the following is a function of the UPSC?

options.d: Conducting examinations for appointments to all-India and Central services

faqs.a: Conducting examinations for appointments to all-India and Central services

faqs.q: The UPSC assists states in framing joint recruitment schemes only when requested by how many states?

options.b: A majority of states in a region

faqs.q: The UPSC serves the needs of a state on the request of the Governor and with whose approval?

options.b: The Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: On which of the following matters is the UPSC consulted and does it advise?

options.a: Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
options.d: Principles for appointments, promotions and transfers in civil services

faqs.a: Principles for appointments, promotions and transfers in civil services

faqs.q: What has the Supreme Court held regarding the effect of a government's failure to consult the UPSC where required?

options.c: The aggrieved public servant has no remedy in court, as the provision is directory not mandatory
options.d: The matter must go to the Election Commission

faqs.a: The aggrieved public servant has no remedy in court, as the provision is directory not mandatory

faqs.q: Does a selection by the UPSC confer any right to the post upon the candidate, as held by the Supreme Court?

options.b: No, it confers no right to the post
options.c: Yes, but only for Group A posts

faqs.a: No, it confers no right to the post

faqs.q: Additional functions relating to Union services can be conferred on the UPSC by which authority?
To whom does the UPSC present its annual performance report?
faqs.e: The President places the report before both Houses of Parliament, along with a memorandum explaining cases where the Commission's advice was not accepted.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding matters outside the functional jurisdiction of the UPSC:
(I) Reservations of appointments for backward classes
(II) Claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in appointments
(III) Appointments to Group A Central services
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The UPSC is not consulted on backward class reservations or SC/ST claims, but Group A appointments generally do fall within its purview.

faqs.q: The UPSC is NOT consulted regarding appointments to which category of Central Services?

Regulations made by the President excluding certain matters from UPSC consultation are known as what?
The Constitution visualises the UPSC as the "watch-dog" of which system in India?
Which department serves as the central personnel agency of India, handling classification of services, pay, cadre management and training — matters outside the UPSC's concern?

options.a: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
options.d: Department of Pensions and Pensioners' Welfare

faqs.e: This is one of three departments under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, created in 1985.

faqs.q: Are the recommendations made by the UPSC binding on the government?

options.a: No, they are only advisory in nature
options.b: Binding only for Group A posts

faqs.a: No, they are only advisory in nature

faqs.q: In which year did the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), whose role sometimes overlaps with the UPSC in disciplinary matters, emerge?
Between the UPSC and the CVC, which body has an edge in case of conflicting advice on disciplinary matters, and why?

options.a: The CVC, since it has statutory status
options.b: The CVC, since it was created earlier
options.c: The UPSC, being an independent constitutional body

faqs.a: The UPSC, being an independent constitutional body
faqs.e: The CVC was created by an executive resolution and given statutory status only in 2003, making it comparatively weaker in standing than the constitutionally established UPSC.

faqs.e: Article 322 deals with Expenses of Public Service Commissions, not Reports; Article 323 deals with Reports.
